participation.context: Walked over with the household and took the draughty end of the bench.
participation.name: William Shakespeare

participation.context: Kept the mud outside, named the sixpence till Lady Day, and wanted quiet after nine.
participation.name: Mistress Dorcas Ansell

participation.context: Greeted the porch and set fourteen heads on the epistle.
participation.name: Master Josias Thwaite

participation.context: Answered for the loom, and took the bench by the pillar.
participation.name: Gillis Verbeke

relations.quote: I never miss a fourteenthly, sir.

relations.note: the back room, and her hours
relations.quote: Only the loom till dusk, and the shuttle makes a small noise.

story.body: You kept to the flags, heard Master Thwaite number fourteen heads and two turnings of the glass, and let Mistress Ansell have the last word on the joists and on quiet after nine. The sixpenny poem is the one you bought on Thursday. You went in at the draughty end.

relations.quote: I never miss a fourteenthly, sir.

relations.note: the back room, and her hours

title: Stood in the porch before morning prayer
